subject: Clarification on Order Form: customer content use, training opt-in & output ownership
messages:
From: Susan Lin <susan.lin@aperture.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@aperture.com
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form: Clarify customer content use & output ownership

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the Order Form and flagged a few key items we need to lock down before we can proceed:

1) Training / Model Use: The current draft says Redwood may use Customer Content for model training unless explicitly opted out. We need a firm, customer-favorable position — Aperture cannot permit any training on sensitive telemetry without explicit opt-in and controls.
2) Output ownership: Need confirmation that Aperture retains ownership of its uploaded content and that downstream productization of Aperture-derived outputs is limited.
3) Feedback license: Procurement asks for clarity on telemetry/feedback — what telemetry is retained, for what purpose, and whether Redwood can use aggregated signals for product improvements.

I've attached a short questionnaire (Aperture_IP_Questions.pdf) and a suggested redline from our legal team. Can your legal/ops folks propose precise clause language we can circulate? Procurement wants a one-page bullet summary and suggested contract language they can run to their GC.

Susan
Legal Ops / Aperture Systems
attachments: Aperture_IP_Questions.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Folks — forwarding Aperture's note (below) and their redline. They want a one-page summary + proposed clause ASAP for procurement.

Ask: can legal propose a concise alternative that preserves our productization freedoms but offers a clear opt-in path for training? Also want an option we can offer in the order form: (A) default: telemetry aggregated only, no training; (B) paid training opt-in with explicit terms.

Priority: Aperture is moving fast on procurement and wants this to go up to their GC next week. Please include a short risks bullet list and recommended commercial alternative (price uplift or credit).

Attachment: aperture_draft_redline.docx (Word doc, redline)

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Clarify customer content use & output ownership — proposed language

Sean / Ben —

Thanks for the ping. Below is a compact recommendation set you can send to Aperture. I've also attached a tracked-change patch for the Order Form (redwood_proposed_orderform_patch.docx). High level: we want to (1) give Aperture a clear opt-out protection in the standard Order Form; (2) keep our ability to productize and improve models via a paid opt-in; and (3) define telemetry/feedback scope.

Recommended one-page bullets for procurement:
- Training: Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train models without Customer's prior written opt-in for such use. We can offer an add-on "Training License" (paid) that grants Redwood limited rights to use customer-provided content to improve models for the customer's benefit. Pricing and retention controls to be agreed in Order Form.
- Output ownership: Customer retains ownership of Customer Content. Outputs generated by Redwood that are solely derivative of Customer Content shall be treated as Customer Data for downstream productization purposes; however, Redwood retains ownership of model weights, architecture, and improvements not uniquely attributable to Customer Content.
- Feedback/Telemetry: Redwood may collect aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvement; telemetry that includes Customer Content or is attributable to customer outputs will not be used for training unless opt-in is provided.

Risk notes (two-line each):
- Commercial risk: Offering free training opt-in reduces monetization path — recommend paid add-on or usage uplift.
- Operational risk: Need retention limits and deletion workflows for opt-in content; engineering/ops impact estimate required (~2-3 sprints for gated ingestion + KMS tagging).

Next steps: send this one-pager to Aperture plus the attached tracked-change Order Form patch. If they accept the high-level, we'll scope the paid Training License (term sheet) and get procurement pricing approval. If Aperture pushes for free training rights, escalate to Marissa for final sign-off on discount exceptions.

Attachment: redwood_proposed_orderform_patch.docx (Word, tracked changes)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference

Hi Susan —

Thanks for the clear note. Laura has proposed language and a short commercial path; I summarized below for your procurement team.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) We send a one-page summary + tracked Order Form redline (attached).
2) Aperture confirms whether it requires a full training opt-out (no training unless customer signs paid add-on) or is open to a paid Training License.
3) If paid add-on is acceptable: Redwood will provide a term sheet (price band + retention controls) for procurement.
4) If Aperture requires free training rights, we will need Marissa's sign-off for any concession/discount.

Attached: redwood_proposed_orderform_patch.docx (please review)

Can you confirm which path Aperture prefers? If you want a sample procurement clause, Laura can send the exact text to your GC.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sean —

Appreciate the fast response and Laura's language. Procurement reviewed the one-pager and has two quick asks: (1) provide a short sample clause (1-2 paragraphs) that we can pass to our GC (Laura said she could provide that); (2) confirm operational retention and deletion controls if we opt-in for training.

Procurement is leaning toward the paid Training License model but wants an estimate of associated uplift and a sample clause for internal approval. They will not accept ambiguous telemetry usage language — they want explicit statements in the Order Form about telemetry de-identification, retention windows, and a contact for data deletion requests.

I've attached their procurement Qs (Aperture_procurement_qs.docx). If you can get Laura's sample clause and a short ops note about retention controls (engineering estimate + contact) by EOD Friday, Procurement will fast-track the GC review.

Susan Lin
Legal Ops / Aperture Systems
